prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules bring a protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell's own machinery removes the protein

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation (B014) with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The decisive point for me is what is chemically new: a designed bifunctional molecule that makes a ternary complex, whose cooperativity and geometry determine whether a protein is ubiquitinated and destroyed, so that action is catalytic and event-driven rather than occupancy-driven. This was conceived and demonstrated by Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto and Kim) in 2001, and made rational and general by Ciulli through VHL ligands, the first fully small-molecule VHL degraders and the ternary-complex crystal structures that showed cooperativity quantitatively. That last step is what makes it a chemistry prize and not only a pharmacology one: the binding thermodynamics can be measured, computed and linked to degradation rates, which is the connection between theory and experiment I look for. Independent laboratories have confirmed it for two decades across many ligases and targets. I answer the chair's first question by saying that I would state the principle in the citation (small-molecule recruitment of an E3 ligase to remove a protein) and not the compound class or clinical outcome, so the prize does not hinge on trial results.
statement.case_against: Two real weaknesses remain and round 1 did not remove them. First, a PROTAC-centred trio omits Handa and Ito, whose identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains an approved drug class, and also omits Sakamoto, Kim and Gray. A reader will see that, and no three-name set avoids it. Second, I still know of no approved heterobifunctional degrader, so the 'already has consequences' test is met by mechanism, breadth of confirmation and clinical programmes rather than by approvals. If the Committee weighs approval heavily, waiting a few years would be defensible, and I accept that argument has force.

responses.point: Heiner argues that the PROTAC and cereblon-glue lineages meet at one principle, that Handa's discovery has a clear date and mechanism and answers the clinical-maturity worry, and that Ciulli's work is largely optimisation after the concept existed. He also asks what Ciulli discovered that is not implied by the others.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously: approved glue-class drugs do show that induced proximity works in patients. But that is an argument about the principle, and the principle is already carried by Crews and Deshaies. What Ciulli adds that is not implied by the others is the structural and thermodynamic basis for designing degraders: VHL ligands, the first fully small-molecule VHL degraders, and ternary-complex structures that explained cooperativity. Without that, PROTACs would be a proof of concept using peptide-based recruitment, not a general chemical method. Handa's cereblon work explains how an existing drug acts, which is a significant mechanistic discovery but a different kind of contribution. I therefore keep Ciulli, and I would word the citation on designed recruitment of E3 ligases and let the report note the glue lineage, rather than stretch one citation over two discoveries.

responses.point: Xiaodong supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa so that one prize covers the heterobifunctional and molecular-glue arms, but concedes that the prize then reads as two lineages stitched together and that a few years of waiting would cost little for PROTACs.
responses.response: Her own case against names the difficulty that I think decides the matter: a trio including Handa joins a mechanism discovery about an existing drug to a design concept, and the citation has to be vague enough to cover both. I agree with her structure-explains-function standard, and I would argue that it supports Ciulli as well, because the ternary-complex structures with VHL are exactly where a small molecule is shown to reshape a ligase surface and create cooperativity. On timing we are close: I do not think the lack of an approved PROTAC is disqualifying after two decades of independent confirmation, but I agree that it is the point on which a reasonable member could vote to wait.

responses.point: Andrei now pairs B014 for Crews and Deshaies only with B042 for Liu alone, to keep each attribution clean and to avoid the three-person trainee unit, while acknowledging that two chemical-biology parts in one year is a cost.
responses.response: I agree with Andrei that Liu alone is a cleaner base-editing attribution than Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and that his two-name PROTAC core is what no one disputes. My disagreement is with using the free seat to add a second part. Dropping Ciulli to make room removes the name that gives the PROTAC part its rational chemistry, and putting two drug-modality parts in one year, both close to the genome-editing and chemical-biology neighbourhood, risks diluting what I regard as the clearest game-changer on the shortlist. Base editing also still has to answer the 2020 CRISPR precedent and the independent Nishida and Kondo work, and I do not think that case is settled yet. I keep B042 as my first alternative and would not oppose it in a later year, with Liu alone.

responses.point: Peter prefers a two-part prize of Buchwald and Hartwig C-N coupling plus Liu alone, and in round 1 conceded that B057 had weak opening support and may look incremental after the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I accept the attribution and maturity argument for C-N coupling: a clean two-name unit with decades of use is as strong as anything on the list. I still read it as a major extension of a family the Committee recognised in 2010, and Peter himself records the incremental risk and the thin opening support. I have therefore not moved it into my configuration, and I note that it is not an alternative I have listed. If the Committee turns to a synthetic-methods prize I would not object, but I would want that discussed explicitly against the 2010 precedent.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee requires an approved heterobifunctional degrader before recognising the PROTAC arm; I judge it is not required but it is the most serious reason to wait.

Whether Ciulli or Handa is the right third name: my judgement rests on design chemistry and ternary-complex structure versus a mechanism discovery, and it would change if the Committee treats induced proximity as a single principle that must include the approved glue arm.
Whether the 2001 contribution of Sakamoto and Kim should be credited ahead of a third name; with a three-name limit I defer to the expert report on priority.
Whether base editing (B042) can show that it is a distinct chemical invention after the 2020 prize, and how the parallel Nishida-Kondo work should be treated.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal for B014. For alternative B030 (Car and Parrinello) I note that it lies in my own field of biomolecular simulation; my Warshel link concerns EVB and the 2013 prize, not this method, and I have not let it affect my ranking. No other disclosure has changed since round 1.
